content: The text provided is a detailed and technical document related to prosthetics and orthotics, focusing on standards, guidelines, and recommendations for service provision, education, training, and policy development. 1. Undergraduate teaching methods for prosthetics and orthotics have been established as a baseline for international comparison, as outlined in the 2015 publication in Prosthetics and Orthotics International (Volume 39, Pages 278–285). 2. Cochrane et al. conducted an impact assessment of prosthetics and orthotics services in India and Bangladesh, with findings accessible in a PDF document as of December 30, 2016. 3. Fisk, Soderberg, Trebbin, Cochrane, and Stills evaluated the outcomes of graduates from the VIETCOT program under the ISPO/LWV framework, with the report available as of August 30, 2016. 4. Sexton, Shangali, and Munissi assessed the impact of training personnel to meet ISPO Category I and II minimum standards in East Africa, specifically in Tanzania, Kenya, and Uganda, with the report accessible as of August 30, 2016. 5. Sexton, Jovane, Rosario, and Castaneda evaluated prosthetics and orthotics services in Latin America, focusing on Mexico, Guatemala, and Colombia, with findings available as of August 30, 2016. 6. Sexton, Stills, Chhoeurn, and Kheng conducted an impact assessment of prosthetics and orthotics services in Southeast Asia, specifically in Cambodia and Lao PDR, with the report accessible as of June 30, 2016. 7. Tardif, Niang, and Amah assessed the impact of prosthetics and orthotics services in West Africa, focusing on Togo and Benin, with findings available as of December 30, 2016. 8. Forghany et al. conducted a scoping review on the influence of staff training and education on the quality of prosthetics and orthotics services, with the study currently in press in Prosthetics and Orthotics International. 9. The International Society for Prosthetics and Orthotics (ISPO) developed a draft education standard for prosthetics and orthotics occupations in 2016, based in Brussels. 10. Guidance for the education of pre-registration physiotherapy students in amputee rehabilitation is available online, with access as of June 30, 2016. 11. Undergraduate medical education in rehabilitation medicine has been documented in a PDF accessible as of June 30, 2016. 12. Geertzen, Rommers, and Dekker developed an ICF-based education program for medical residents in amputation rehabilitation in the Netherlands, published in Prosthetics and Orthotics International in 2011 (Volume 35, Pages 318–322). 13. Evidence-based clinical guidelines for the physiotherapy management of adults with lower limb prostheses are available in a PDF document, accessed as of June 30, 2016. 14. Standards and guidelines for amputee and prosthetic rehabilitation are documented in a PDF accessible as of June 30, 2016. 15. The ISPO consensus conference on poliomyelitis produced consensus statements published in Prosthetics and Orthotics International in 2001 (Volume 25, Issue 3, Pages 171–180). 16. A consensus conference report on the orthotic management of stroke patients is available online, accessed as of June 30, 2016. 17. The ISPO cerebral palsy consensus conference report was published in Prosthetics and Orthotics International in 2009 (Volume 33, Issue 4, Pages 401–402). 18. Kilbride developed practice guidelines for occupational therapists and physiotherapists on splinting for the prevention and correction of contractures in adults with neurological dysfunction, published in London in 2015. 19. Magnusson and Ramstrand explored the educational experience and professional development of prosthetists/orthotists in Pakistan, published in Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology in 2009 (Volume 4, Pages 385–392). 20. Magnusson and Ahlström documented the experiences of local staff providing prosthetics and orthotics services in Sierra Leone, published in Disability and Rehabilitation in 2012 (Volume 34, Pages 2111–2118). 21. Magnusson, Shangali, and GA examined graduates’ perceptions of prosthetics and orthotics education and clinical practice in Tanzania and Malawi, published in the African Journal of Disability in 2016 (Volume 5, Article a142). 22. DaVanzo et al. analyzed the adequacy of the workforce supply to meet patient demand in the orthotics and prosthetics profession, published by Dobson DaVanzo & Associates in Vienna, VA, in 2015. 23. Seccombe and Stock examined the labor market for qualified orthotists/prosthetists, published in Health Trends in 1994 (Volume 26, Pages 53–56). 24. Ridgewell et al. analyzed the demographics of the Australian orthotics and prosthetics workforce in 2007, published in the Australian Health Review in 2016 (Volume 40, Pages 555–561). 25. The British Association of Prosthetists and Orthotists (BAPO) developed a guidance paper on the supervision of assistant practitioners, with standards for best practice accessible as of June 30, 2016. 26. Strategies to increase access to health workers in remote and rural areas through improved retention are documented in a PDF accessible as of December 30, 2016. 27. Skempes and Bickenbach emphasized strengthening rehabilitation for people with disabilities using a human rights approach, published in the American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation in 2015 (Volume 94, Pages 823–828). 28. The American Geriatrics Society Expert Panel on Person-Centered Care defined and outlined essential elements of person-centered care, published in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society in 2016 (Volume 64, Pages 15–18). 29. Healy et al. conducted a systematic review on the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of prosthetic and orthotic interventions, published by the Centre for Reviews and Dissemination at the University of York in 2016. 30. The relationship between prosthetics and orthotics services and community-based rehabilitation was outlined in a joint ISPO/WHO statement in October 1999, accessible as of June 30, 2016. 31. A handbook on architectural programming for physical rehabilitation centers is available online, accessed as of June 30, 2016. 32. Negrini et al. conducted a prospective study on the effectiveness of combined bracing and exercise in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, published in BMC Musculoskeletal Disorders in 2014 (Volume 15, Article 263). 33. Boddington et al. developed a framework for planning, monitoring, and evaluating prosthetics and orthotics programs, published by ISPO in Copenhagen in 2004. 34. Bosmans, Geertzen, and Dijkstra assessed consumer satisfaction with prosthetics and orthotics services, published in Prosthetics and Orthotics International in 2009 (Volume 33, Pages 69–77).
